sources.citation: Parakh, Mona. 2019. Preliminary Phonological Description of Rathvi. Language in India 19(4), April 2019: 266-275.
sources.note: Describes a DIFFERENT variety: Rathvi of the Rathwa of Chhota Udepur/Jabugam/Nasvadi, Gujarat (= Glottolog rath1243 Rathawi [rtw], Bhilali cluster). Segmental inventory only; sec. 6.1: 'Based on a cursory observation it appears that vowels in Rathvi get relatively longer when they occur in stressed syllables. However, length of vowels and the stress pattern of Rathvi have not been dealt within this work.' No placement rule.

sources.citation: Varkey, Vinod Wilson & Kishore Kumar Vunnamatla. 2018. A Sociolinguistic Study of Bareli/Pauri and Related Languages. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2018-011. Dallas: SIL International. 197 pp.
sources.note: Silent. Defines the Rathwi cluster (Rathwi Bareli wordlists from Tharadpura, Udainagar, Chiklia, Chenpur, Dongargaon; Rathwi Pauri from Amalwadi, Segwi; RTT at Budi); wordlists are 'field transcriptions [that] have not undergone thorough phonological and grammatical analysis'; 'accent' occurs only in SRT proficiency-level descriptors.

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. 1907. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX: Indo-Aryan Family, Central Group, Part III: The Bhil Languages, including Khandesi, Banjari or Labhani, Bahrupia, &c. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing. Sections 'Bhili of Ali Rajpur and Barwani' (pp. 61-62, 'in Barwani, Rathvi Bhilali'), 'Bhilali of Barwani' and 'Rathvi Bhilali dialect (Barwani State)' specimens Nos. 15-16 (pp. 67-68), 'Barel' of Chhota Udepur (pp. 69-70).
sources.note: Nothing. Pronunciation notes cover broad a, palatals, v>b, cerebral l, nasalization, r-drop, pleonastic -lo; Barwani Bhilali/Rathvi Bhilali 'essentially identical with the dialect spoken in Ali Rajpur, and they do not call for any separate remarks'. Only the volume front matter has a transcription convention ('when it is necessary to mark an accented syllable, the acute accent is used', illustrated with Khowar), never applied to any Bhil dialect.
